declarations.name: Lemma M1. A single contact enlarges either other component
declarations.scope: In every mixed full-cycle DT/3-cycle tree, a unique support contact of a DT with T=(abc) at a permits Q^2 and Q^-2, after cut-preserving literal gathering, to enlarge respectively either other complementary component. At a global maximum, the contact can therefore occur only in a unique largest component.

declarations.name: Lemma M2. Complementary twists synchronize equal component trees
declarations.scope: At a global maximum of the largest T-cut component, complementary full twists preserve the same three roots/cycles. Internal DTs in a component not uniquely largest are impossible. Edge-pairings incident to such a component require equal component sizes and the same rooted cyclic edge bijection; pairing a smaller component with a unique largest is impossible. These constraints reapply after every complementary braid.

declarations.name: Lemma M3. A unique largest component forces isolation
declarations.scope: At a global maximum, a unique largest T-cut component forces both other components to be singletons. Otherwise two equal smaller trees are synchronized, a paired exclusive-leaf DT is aligned at both roots, and Q^2 enlarges the largest component by s-1.

declarations.name: Lemma M4. Three equal nontrivial components are impossible
declarations.scope: Three equal nontrivial T-cut components are impossible at the maximum. Each DT pairs two equal component trees; all three types have (q-1)/2 factors. Different projected edge types cannot share a vertex, by a literal pair conjugation violating the same cyclic matching. Their two-type component tree would then be disconnected.

declarations.name: Lemma M5. The two-largest tie has a uniform seven-sheet escape
declarations.scope: For the two-largest tie at the maximum, the third component is a singleton and the two equal q-vertex trees are synchronized. For q>=3, diagonal transposition Hurwitz moves normalize to paired stars and the literal word (-1,-1,-1,2,2) on T and two satellites creates two exclusive T leaves. All outside satellites are explicitly fixed.

declarations.name: Theorem M6. Mixed-factor isolation and its exact boundary
declarations.scope: For every mixed full-cycle tuple on odd N>=7 with one 3-cycle and all other factors DTs, some full braid representative has two exclusive leaves of the 3-cycle; deleting it and those leaves leaves a pure-DT full-cycle tuple on N-2 sheets. At N=3 this is trivial. At N=5 it is impossible, and every tuple has cuts (1,2,2). No monodromy hypothesis is required.

declarations.name: Theorem M7. All-degree mixed connectivity, extraction and restoration
declarations.scope: For every odd N>=3, the full-cycle mixed domain has one literal unmarked braid orbit and one exactly first-marked orbit; its absolute quotient is also connected. Every N>=5 orbit has a removable DT. Arbitrary two-fresh-leaf DT extensions of a mixed tuple, starting with A3, restore to the unique mixed component. Isolated 3-cycle extensions of any pure-DT core have no additional anchor or orientation orbit. The proof uses universal T isolation, the pure classification, and the separate complete mixed degree-nine base.
